q: Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the lamp. If a lamp is moved from 10 cm to 20 cm away, how does the light intensity change?
explanation: I ∝ 1/d². Doubling the distance gives (10 ÷ 20)² = ¼ of the original intensity; at 30 cm it would be (10 ÷ 30)² = 1/9. So when plotting rate against light intensity, use 1/d² (not distance) on the x-axis, or the curve will look misleading.
